Referral Note

Referred for psychiatric evaluation. Ms. Whitfield has had recurring episodes of depression that lift and then return, and she is in another one now. I feel the pattern needs specialist assessment. I have deliberately held off on starting a new medication until she has been evaluated. Please provide a diagnostic assessment and treatment recommendations; I will continue to follow her for primary care.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Neatly dressed in business-casual clothes (blazer over a sweater) and well groomed; appears stated age. No visible scars.

Behavior: Cooperative and engaged. Fair eye contact that drops when she describes the low periods. Mild psychomotor slowing; no agitation.

Speech: Normal rate and volume, somewhat reduced spontaneity. Briefly more animated, but not pressured, when describing the energetic periods.

Mood / Affect: Mood “mostly depressed lately.” Affect mildly restricted and congruent; brightens briefly when she talks about feeling “amazing.”

Thought / Perception: Logical, organized and goal-directed. No hallucinations or delusions. Denies suicidal and homicidal ideation.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and oriented ×4; attention and memory grossly intact. Insight and judgment intact, though she regards the energetic periods as welcome rather than as symptoms.
